prompt:
Read the user's English, Swedish, or German news paragraph and return every company named in it. Output only a JSON array of strings: no object wrapper, Markdown, comments, explanations, or questions. If there are no named companies, output [].

Include businesses named directly or only through a product or service, a possessive, a website, or an email domain. Exclude people and their titles, cities, regions, countries, product categories, generic descriptions, and businesses that are not named. Do not infer additional businesses from outside knowledge.

Strip a trailing legal-form suffix from this list, with or without a final period: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, PLC, Inc., LLC, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V. Retain words belonging to the name, such as Group, Systems, Labs, Partners, Works, Freight, Energy, and Foods.

When a product or service name combines a company name with a product word, return the company name alone, even without a standalone mention. Multiple products from one parent yield one entry. Remove English possessive endings written with either apostrophe style and Swedish or German genitive -s, keeping any s that is part of the name.

A web address or email domain names its owner. If that company is named elsewhere in the paragraph, use its name from the paragraph. Otherwise take the part before the top-level domain, excluding www. or the email local part, and capitalise its first letter. Preserve capitalisation and diacritics in names written in the paragraph. Never translate, abbreviate, or ASCII-fold them.

Scan the entire paragraph for all mention forms. Deduplicate by company and order entries by earliest mention in any form.

Worked example
Input: "Auf www.noervaq.de erschien zunächst eine Mitteilung über Kühlgeräte. Später bestätigte Nöervaq GmbH den Bericht. Zembryqs Sprecher kündigte an, dass Zembryq Scan und Zembryq Vault getrennt angeboten werden. Rückfragen beantwortete press@vulnexa.de."
Output: ["Nöervaq", "Zembryq", "Vulnexa"]
